title: Bounded Subgroups of Reductive Groups over Local Fields
body_html:
Bounded Subgroups of Reductive Groups over Local Fields

Let \(G\) be a connected reductive group over a non-archimedean local field \(F\) with valuation ring \(\mathcal{O}_F\), maximal ideal \(\mathfrak{p}_F\), and residue field \(\mathbb{F}_q\). The compact open subgroups of \(G(F)\) — the bounded subgroups — are the primary objects organized by the Bruhat-Tits building.

Definition

A subgroup \(K \subseteq G(F)\) is bounded if one (equivalently, all) of the following equivalent conditions holds:

  1. Functional boundedness. For every regular function \(f \in \mathcal{O}(G)\), the set \(f(K) \subseteq F\) is bounded: \(\sup_{g \in K} \lvert f(g)\rvert_F < \infty\).

  2. Cocharacter test. For every cocharacter \(\lambda : \mathbb{G}_m \to G\) and every \(g \in K\), the element \(\lambda(t) g \lambda(t)^{-1}\) extends to a function that remains bounded as \(t \to 0\) and as \(t \to \infty\); this conjugation does not blow up in either direction.

  3. Topological. The closure \(\overline{K}\) in \(G(F)\) (with its locally compact topology) is compact.

  4. Integral model. There exists a smooth affine \(\mathcal{O}_F\)-group scheme \(\mathcal{G}\) with generic fibre \(G\) such that \(K \subseteq \mathcal{G}(\mathcal{O}_F)\).

For \(G = \mathrm{GL}_n\), these agree: \(K \subseteq \mathrm{GL}_n(F)\) is bounded iff there exists \(c \in F^\times\) such that \(K \subseteq \mathrm{GL}_n(c \cdot \mathcal{O}_F)\).

The \(G(F)^1\) subgroup

Define the canonical subgroup \[ G(F)^1 \;:=\; \{g \in G(F) : \omega(\chi(g)) = 0 \text{ for all } \chi \in X^*(G)\}, \] where \(\omega : F \to \mathbb{R} \cup \{\infty\}\) is the non-archimedean valuation extended to an algebraic closure. This is a characteristic open normal subgroup of \(G(F)\) that: - Contains every bounded subgroup of \(G(F)\). - Equals \(G(F)\) when the maximal split central torus \(A_G\) of \(G\) is trivial. - Has a quotient \(G(F) / G(F)^1 \cong X^*(G) \otimes_{\mathbb{Z}} \mathbb{R}\) (or a discrete subgroup thereof), trivial when \(G\) is semisimple.

Structure theorem

Theorem (Bruhat-Tits, Kaletha-Prasad §2.2). Let \(G\) be a connected reductive group over a non-archimedean local field \(F\).

  1. Boundedness criterion. A subgroup \(K \subseteq G(F)^1\) is bounded if and only if the \(K\)-orbit of every point in the Bruhat-Tits building \(\mathcal{B}(G, F)\) is bounded (with respect to the canonical metric).

  2. Fixed-point theorem (Bruhat-Tits). Every bounded subgroup of \(G(F)\) fixes a point in the enlarged building \(\tilde{\mathcal{B}}(G, F)\), and every bounded subgroup of \(G(F)^1\) fixes a point in the reduced building \(\mathcal{B}(G, F)\).

  3. Maximal compact subgroups. Every maximal bounded subgroup of \(G(F)^1\) is of the form \(G(F)^1_x\) (stabilizer of some point \(x \in \mathcal{B}(G, F)\)).

  4. Finitely many conjugacy classes. The maximal bounded subgroups of \(G(F)^1\) form finitely many conjugacy classes, corresponding to the \(G(F)^1\)-orbits on the set of vertices of \(\mathcal{B}(G, F)\).

Examples

Group Bounded subgroups
\(\mathrm{GL}_n(F)\) Conjugates of \(\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal{O}_F)\); \(n+1\) conjugacy classes of max. bounded subgroups when \(F = \mathbb{Q}_p\)
\(\mathrm{SL}_2(F)\) Two conjugacy classes: \(\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_F)\) and its conjugate under \(\begin{pmatrix}\pi & 0\\ 0 & 1\end{pmatrix}\)
\(\mathrm{SL}_2(F)\) unramified quasi-split If \(G\) is unramified, the hyperspecial vertices have a single conjugacy class
Anisotropic \(G\) \(G(F)\) itself is bounded (and hence compact)

Comparison with the archimedean case

Over \(\mathbb{R}\), the analogue is the following: bounded subgroups of a real Lie group \(H(\mathbb{R})\) are the relatively compact subgroups, and maximal compact subgroups are the stabilizers of points of the symmetric space \(X = H(\mathbb{R})/K\). The Cartan fixed-point theorem (bounded subgroup of an isometry group of a non-positively curved space fixes a point) is the archimedean analogue of the Bruhat-Tits fixed-point theorem.

Kottwitz homomorphism

For connected reductive \(G\), the Kottwitz homomorphism \(\kappa_G : G(F) \to X^*(Z(\hat G))_{\Gamma}\) (the coinvariants of the dual group's centre) factors through \(G(F)/G(F)^1\). A subgroup \(K \subseteq G(F)\) is bounded iff it is contained in the kernel of \(\kappa_G\), i.e.\ \(K \subseteq G(F)^1\) and \(K\) is compact. See parahoric subgroups for the role of boundedness in the definition of parahorics.
